messages.subject: Ploting Matrix - problem with scale and order of objects(labels)
parts:
Hi,

I would like to use ggplot2 to print correlation matrix with
labels of metabolites on X and Y axis.

What I do now is

# Calculate correlation
cor <- cor(subject);
library(ggplot2);
# Reorder columns by class name of molecule
reacols = order(toupper(gsub("[C]*[_0-9]", "\\2",
colnames(cor), perl=TRUE)));
rearows = order(toupper(gsub("[C]*[_0-9]", "\\2",
rownames(cor), perl=TRUE)));
cor =
cor[c(rearows),c(reacols)];
# Melt for use with ggplot2
cor <- melt(cor);
p <- ggplot(cor, aes(X1, X2)) + geom_tile(aes(fill = value),
colour = "white") + scale_fill_gradient(low = "blue", high = "red");
base_size <- 9;
p + theme_grey(base_size = base_size) + labs(x = "", y = "") +
scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) + scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0,
0)) + opts(legend.position = "right", axis.ticks = theme_blank(),
axis.text.x = theme_text(size = base_size * 0.8, angle = 290, hjust =
0, colour = "grey50"))

The problem I have are:

1) The scale is from blue to red with zero correlation as
purple. Is it possible to make zero correlation white, red possitive
and blue negative ? (three point scale)
2) The most important however is that I want the metabolties
on X and Y axis to be ordered by classification (biological) however I
see that after using melt(...) they're properly ordered, however when
I want to plot them, they're again mixed up.

For any help, thanks in advance
Mateusz

parts:
Hi,

As for the order of category, the order in data.frame has no effect,
but the order of the levels of the factor can determine it. use
gregmisc::reorder.factor
and as for the second point, you need to use scale_fill_gradient2, not
colour, because the tiles are filled.
try the following modifications:

# Order again groups
#meltcormat = meltcormat[order(meltcormat[,1]),];
#meltcormat = meltcormat[order(meltcormat[,2]),];

library(gregmisc) ## is necessary to re-order the levels of factor
meltcormat[,1]<-reorder(meltcormat[,1],c(paste("A",1:3),
paste("B",4:5), paste("C",6:10)))
meltcormat[,2]<-reorder(meltcormat[,2],c(paste("A",1:3),
paste("B",4:5), paste("C",6:10)))

#p <- ggplot(meltcormat, aes(X1, X2)) + geom_tile(aes(fill = value),

colour = "white") +
scale_colour_gradient2(low="blue",mid="white",high="red");
p <- ggplot(meltcormat, aes(X1, X2)) + geom_tile(aes(fill = value),
colour = "white") +

scale_fill_gradient2(low="blue",mid="white",high="red");

HTH.

messages.subject: Re: Ploting Matrix - problem with scale and order of objects(labels)
parts:
Dear Takahashi,

The following code to plot correlation matrix using ggplot2 (with Your suggestion) does exactly what I expected, a big thanks.

library(ggplot2); ## use ggplot2
# Create 10x10 matrix with random numbers

matrix = runif(100);
dim(matrix) <- c(10,10);

# Three different groups A, B, C are in order and so they should be in correlation matrix
colnames(matrix) <- c(paste("A",1:3), paste("B",4:5), paste("C",6:10));
# Calculate Pearson's correlation and vectorize (melt) it.

cormat <- cor(matrix);
meltcormat <- melt(cormat);
# Order groups by strings

#meltcormat = meltcormat[order(meltcormat[,1]),];
#meltcormat = meltcormat[order(meltcormat[,2]),];
# Instead

library(gregmisc) ## is necessary to re-order the levels of factor
meltcormat[,1]<-reorder(meltcormat[,1],c(paste("A",1:3),
paste("B",4:5), paste("C",6:10)))
meltcormat[,2]<-reorder(meltcormat[,2],c(paste("A",1:3),
paste("B",4:5), paste("C",6:10)))
p <- ggplot(meltcormat, aes(X1, X2)) + geom_tile(aes(fill = value), colour = "white") + scale_fill_gradient2(low="blue",mid="white",high="red");
# Adjust theme

base_size <- 9;
p + theme_grey(base_size = base_size) + labs(x = "", y = "") + scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) + scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0,0)) + opts(legend.position = "right", axis.ticks = theme_blank(), axis.text.x = theme_text(size = base_size * 0.8, angle = 290, hjust =0, colour = "grey50"))

Hi Mateusz,

As Takahashi said: "As for the order of category, the order in

data.frame has no effect,
but the order of the levels of the factor can determine it. "

The order of your data is basically immaterial - if you want to
control the order of the labels on the axes you either need to use
factors or specify the limits of the underlying scale.

Hadley
